dt_guide.text: {greeting} Donegal Castle. The O'Donnells built the tower in the 1400s. When they fled to Europe in 1607, the Flight of the Earls, the English moved in and Sir Basil Brooke built himself a fine manor on the side.
Go on in. Mind the fireplace; it's carved with Brooke's coat of arms, and he was not a modest man.

dt_waterbus.text: The Waterbus! Round Donegal Bay with the seals and the islands, and a running commentary from me, whether you like it or not.
Out west there's Killybegs, Ireland's biggest fishing port, and past that the cliffs of Slieve League, near six hundred metres straight down to the sea. Taller than three Blackpool Towers.

dt_farmer.text: The Diamond was the market square. Fair days, the whole county came in with cattle and sheep and opinions, and left with less of all three.

dt_teen.text: There's nothing to do in Donegal Town. Except the castle. And the bay. And the waterbus. And the chipper. Fine, there's a few things.

then.text: I'll be on the Tory boat. My grandmother says I'll be sick the whole way. My grandmother is usually right.
A crowning on Tory? With a céilí? Say no more. Well, say a bit more, what are they paying? Nothing? Grand, I'm in.
And the fiddler from Gaoth Dobhair's coming too? Then we're a band. Away and tell them on Tory.

else.text: You'll need a fiddler too. There's one in the pub in Gaoth Dobhair who plays mazurkas like the floor's on fire.
This is a button accordion. Push for one note, pull for another. It's like a conversation with a very loud lung.
In Donegal we had the fiddle first, the box came later, and they've been arguing about tempo ever since.

then.text: Tell Bernie I'll ring her. She'll be raging I've eaten it already.
Is that from Bernie? A cake! She remembered. She never remembers.
I live here and work in Derry three days a week. Over and back on the same road, no passport, no bother. That's the Common Travel Area.
It's been going since 1923: the UK, Ireland, Man and the Channel Islands. British and Irish citizens can live, work, study and see a doctor in either.
Irish citizens living in the UK can vote there, and my English neighbour votes for the Dáil here. Very seriously. He reads the leaflets.
Mind, I'm paid in pounds and I shop in euros. My purse has two pockets and a grudge.
Noted in the Gazetteer, under How these isles work.
Take this card back to Bernie, would you? She'll cry. Then she'll deny it.

else.text: {greeting} Lovely day for it, whatever it is. My sister's a baker in Derry, if you're ever over that way.
